sanskrit: brāhmaṇānāṃ mahārāja ceṣṭāḥ saṃsiddhikārikāḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ ca vakṣyāmi tavāpi viditaṃ punaḥ
english: Such, O great king, are the pursuits that bring the brāhmaṇas to perfection; and now I shall declare those of the kṣatriyas as well, though they are already known to you.

sanskrit: yajño vidyā samutthānam asaṃtoṣaḥ śriyaṃ prati daṇḍadhāraṇam atyugraṃ prajānāṃ paripālanam
english: Sacrifice, learning, exertion, a refusal to rest content in the pursuit of fortune, the wielding of stern punishment, and the protection of the subjects—

sanskrit: vedajñānaṃ tathā kṛtsnaṃ tapaḥ sucaritaṃ tathā draviṇopārjanaṃ bhūri pātreṣu pratipādanam
english: the full knowledge of the Veda, austerity well practised, the amassing of abundant wealth, and the bestowing of it upon worthy recipients—

sanskrit: etāni rājñāṃ karmāṇi sukṛtāni viśāṃ pate imaṃ lokam amuṃ lokaṃ sādhayantīti naḥ śrutam
english: these are the deeds of kings, O lord of peoples, and when well performed, so we have heard, they secure for them both this world and the next.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ jyāyas tu kaunteya daṇḍadhāraṇam ucyate balaṃ hi kṣatriye nityaṃ bale daṇḍaḥ samāhitaḥ
english: Among these, O son of Kuntī, the wielding of punishment is called the highest; for strength abides ever in the kṣatriya, and in strength the rod of chastisement is grounded.

sanskrit: etāś ceṣṭāḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ rājan saṃsiddhikārikāḥ api gāthām imāṃ cāpi bṛhaspatir abhāṣata
english: These, O king, are the pursuits that bring the kṣatriyas to perfection; and upon this very theme Bṛhaspati also spoke this verse:

sanskrit: bhūmir etau nigirati sarpo bilaśayān iva rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam
english: "The earth swallows up these two, as a serpent swallows the creatures that dwell in its hole: the king who will not give battle, and the brāhmaṇa who will not go forth to wander."

sanskrit: sudyumnaś cāpi rājarṣiḥ śrūyate daṇḍadhāraṇāt prāptavān paramāṃ siddhiṃ dakṣaḥ prācetaso yathā
english: And the royal sage Sudyumna too, we have heard, attained the supreme perfection through the wielding of punishment, even as Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, attained it.

sanskrit: yudhiṣṭhira uvāca bhagavan karmaṇā kena sudyumno vasudhādhipaḥ saṃsiddhiṃ paramāṃ prāptaḥ śrotum icchāmi taṃ nṛpam
english: Yudhiṣṭhira said: Holy one, by what deed did Sudyumna, that lord of the earth, attain the supreme perfection? I wish to hear of that king.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca atrāpy udāharantīmam itihāsaṃ purātanam śaṅkhaś ca likhitaś cāstāṃ bhrātarau saṃyatavratau
english: Vyāsa said: On this point too they recount an ancient tale. There were two brothers, Śaṅkha and Likhita, both steadfast in their vows.

sanskrit: tayor āvasathāv āstāṃ ramaṇīyau pṛthak pṛthak nityapuṣpaphalair vṛkṣair upetau bāhudām anu
english: The two of them had their dwellings, lovely and set apart from each other, furnished with trees ever in flower and fruit, along the river Bāhudā.

sanskrit: tataḥ kadā cil likhitaḥ śaṅkhasyāśramam āgamat yadṛcchayāpi śaṅkho 'tha niṣkrānto 'bhavad āśramāt
english: Now once it happened that Likhita came to the hermitage of Śaṅkha; and Śaṅkha, as chance would have it, had gone forth from his hermitage.

sanskrit: so 'bhigamyāśramaṃ bhrātuḥ śaṅkhasya likhitas tadā phalāni śātayām āsa samyak pariṇatāny uta
english: Then Likhita, having come to the hermitage of his brother Śaṅkha, plucked down some fruits that were fully ripe.

sanskrit: tāny upādāya visrabdho bhakṣayām āsa sa dvijaḥ tasmiṃś ca bhakṣayaty eva śaṅkho 'py āśramam āgamat
english: Taking them up, the twice-born one ate them without misgiving; and even as he was eating, Śaṅkha returned to the hermitage.

sanskrit: bhakṣayantaṃ tu taṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkho bhrātaram abravīt kutaḥ phalāny avāptāni hetunā kena khādasi
english: Seeing his brother eating, Śaṅkha said to him: "Whence did you obtain these fruits? By what right do you eat them?"

sanskrit: so 'bravīd bhrātaraṃ jyeṣṭham upaspṛśyābhivādya ca ita eva gṛhītāni mayeti prahasann iva
english: Touching water and saluting his elder brother, he replied, as though with a smile: "They were taken by me from this very place."

sanskrit: tam abravīt tadā śaṅkhas tīvrakopasamanvitaḥ steyaṃ tvayā kṛtam idaṃ phalāny ādadatā svayam gaccha rājānam āsādya svakarma prathayasva vai
english: Then Śaṅkha, filled with sharp wrath, said to him: "This is theft you have done, taking the fruits of your own accord. Go, present yourself before the king, and make your deed known."

sanskrit: adattādānam evedaṃ kṛtaṃ pārthivasattama stenaṃ māṃ tvaṃ viditvā ca svadharmam anupālaya śīghraṃ dhāraya caurasya mama daṇḍaṃ narādhipa
english: "Say: 'O best of kings, this that I have done is the taking of what was not given. Knowing me to be a thief, observe your own duty: swiftly inflict, O lord of men, the punishment due to me, a thief.'"

sanskrit: ity uktas tasya vacanāt sudyumnaṃ vasudhādhipam abhyagacchan mahābāho likhitaḥ saṃśitavrataḥ
english: Thus addressed, and in obedience to his word, O mighty-armed one, Likhita, firm in his vow, went up to Sudyumna, the lord of the earth.

sanskrit: sudyumnas tv antapālebhyaḥ śrutvā likhitam āgatam abhyagacchat sahāmātyaḥ padbhyām eva nareśvaraḥ
english: And Sudyumna, hearing from his frontier-guards that Likhita had come, went out to meet him on foot, together with his ministers, that lord of men.

sanskrit: tam abravīt samāgatya sa rājā brahmavittamam kim āgamanam ācakṣva bhagavan kṛtam eva tat
english: Coming up to that best of those who know the brahman, the king said to him: "Tell me the reason for your coming, holy one; whatever it be, consider it already done."

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ sa viprarṣiḥ sudyumnam idam abravīt pratiśrauṣi kariṣyeti śrutvā tat kartum arhasi
english: Thus addressed, the sage among brāhmaṇas said this to Sudyumna: "You have promised that you will do it; having heard my request, you must perform it."

sanskrit: anisṛṣṭāni guruṇā phalāni puruṣarṣabha bhakṣitāni mayā rājaṃs tatra māṃ śādhi māciram
english: "Fruits not granted by my elder, O bull among men, were eaten by me; for that, O king, chastise me, and do not delay."

sanskrit: sudyumna uvāca pramāṇaṃ cen mato rājā bhavato daṇḍadhāraṇe anujñāyām api tathā hetuḥ syād brāhmaṇarṣabha
english: Sudyumna said: If the king is held by you to be the authority in the matter of inflicting punishment, then, O bull among brāhmaṇas, he must equally be the authority in the matter of pardon.

sanskrit: sa bhavān abhyanujñātaḥ śucikarmā mahāvrataḥ brūhi kāmān ato 'nyāṃs tvaṃ kariṣyāmi hi te vacaḥ
english: You, whose deeds are pure and whose vows are great, are hereby pardoned. Name some other desire, and I shall do as you bid.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca chandyamāno 'pi brahmarṣiḥ pārthivena mahātmanā nānyaṃ vai varayām āsa tasmād daṇḍād ṛte varam
english: Vyāsa said: But the brahman-sage, though urged by the great-souled king, would choose no other boon save that punishment alone.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa pṛthivīpālo likhitasya mahātmanaḥ karau pracchedayām āsa dhṛtadaṇḍo jagāma saḥ
english: Thereupon the guardian of the earth had the two hands of the great-souled Likhita cut off; and he, having received his punishment, departed.

sanskrit: sa gatvā bhrātaraṃ śaṅkham ārtarūpo 'bravīd idam dhṛtadaṇḍasya durbhuddher bhagavan kṣantum arhasi
english: Going to his brother Śaṅkha, he said this in his distress: "I have received my punishment; pardon now, holy one, your foolish brother."

sanskrit: śaṅkha uvāca na kupye tava dharmajña na ca dūṣayase mama dharmas tu te vyatikrāntas tatas te niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā
english: Śaṅkha said: I am not angry with you, O knower of duty, nor have you wronged me; but your duty had been transgressed, and now your expiation has been made.

sanskrit: sa gatvā bāhudāṃ śīghraṃ tarpayasva yathāvidhi devān pitṝn ṛṣīṃś caiva mā cādharme manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: Go swiftly to the Bāhudā and offer there, as the rite prescribes, the water-libations to the gods, the fathers, and the seers; and set not your mind upon unrighteousness.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca tasya tad vacanaṃ śrutvā śaṅkhasya likhitas tadā avagāhyāpagāṃ puṇyām udakārthaṃ pracakrame
english: Vyāsa said: Hearing those words of Śaṅkha, Likhita then plunged into the holy river and set about the offering of water.

sanskrit: prādurāstāṃ tatas tasya karau jalajasaṃnibhau tataḥ sa vismito bhrātur darśayām āsa tau karau
english: Thereupon his two hands appeared again, as fair as lotuses risen from the water; and in wonder he showed those hands to his brother.

sanskrit: tatas tam abravīc chaṅkhas tapasedaṃ kṛtaṃ mayā mā ca te 'tra viśaṅkā bhūd daivam eva vidhīyate
english: Then Śaṅkha said to him: "This was wrought by me through my austerity. Let there be no doubt in you on this account—it is the divine will alone that is here ordained."

sanskrit: likhita uvāca kiṃ nu nāhaṃ tvayā pūtaḥ pūrvam eva mahādyute yasya te tapaso vīryam īdṛśaṃ dvijasattama
english: Likhita said: Why then, O greatly resplendent one, did you not purify me at the very first, you whose austerity has such power, O best of the twice-born?

sanskrit: śaṅkha uvāca evam etan mayā kāryaṃ nāhaṃ daṇḍadharas tava sa ca pūto narapatis tvaṃ cāpi pitṛbhiḥ saha
english: Śaṅkha said: Thus it was for me to do; I am not the wielder of punishment over you. And now that lord of men is purified, and so too are you, together with the fathers.

sanskrit: vyāsa uvāca sa rājā pāṇḍavaśreṣṭha śreṣṭho vai tena karmaṇā prāptavān paramāṃ siddhiṃ dakṣaḥ prācetaso yathā
english: Vyāsa said: That king, O best of the Pāṇḍavas, made foremost by that deed, attained the supreme perfection, even as Dakṣa, son of Pracetas, attained it.

sanskrit: eṣa dharmaḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ prajānāṃ paripālanam utpathe 'smin mahārāja mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ
english: This is the duty of kṣatriyas—the protection of the subjects who stray from the path, O great king. Do not, therefore, set your mind upon grief.

sanskrit: bhrātur asya hitaṃ vākyaṃ śṛṇu dharmajñasattama daṇḍa eva hi rājendra kṣatradharmo na muṇḍanam
english: Hear the wholesome counsel of your brother here, O best of those who know duty: it is punishment indeed, O lord of kings, that is the kṣatriya's law, not the shaving of one's head as an ascetic.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca punar eva maharṣis taṃ kṛṣṇadvaipāyano 'bravīt ajātaśatruṃ kaunteyam idaṃ vacanam arthavat
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Once more the great seer Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana spoke this weighty word to Ajātaśatru, the son of Kuntī:

sanskrit: araṇye vasatāṃ tāta bhrātṝṇāṃ te tapasvinām manorathā mahārāja ye tatrāsan yudhiṣṭhira
english: Dear son, those longings that your austere brothers cherished, O great king Yudhiṣṭhira, while they dwelt in the forest—

sanskrit: tān ime bharataśreṣṭha prāpnuvantu mahārathāḥ praśādhi pṛthivīṃ pārtha yayātir iva nāhuṣaḥ
english: let these mighty warriors, O best of the Bhāratas, now attain them. Rule the earth, O Pārtha, as Yayāti, the son of Nahuṣa, ruled it.

sanskrit: araṇye duḥkhavasatir anubhūtā tapasvibhiḥ duḥkhasyānte naravyāghrāḥ sukhaṃ tv anubhavantv ime
english: A sorrowful sojourn in the forest has been endured by these austere men; now, at the end of their sorrow, let these tigers among men taste happiness.

sanskrit: dharmam arthaṃ ca kāmaṃ ca bhrātṛbhiḥ saha bhārata anubhūya tataḥ paścāt prasthātāsi viśāṃ pate
english: Having enjoyed righteousness, profit, and pleasure together with your brothers, O Bhārata, then afterwards you may set forth, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: atithīnāṃ ca pitṝṇāṃ devatānāṃ ca bhārata ānṛṇyaṃ gaccha kaunteya tataḥ svargaṃ gamiṣyasi
english: Discharge your debt to guests, to the fathers, and to the gods, O Bhārata, son of Kuntī; then will you go to heaven.

sanskrit: sarvamedhāśvamedhābhyāṃ yajasva kurunandana tataḥ paścān mahārāja gamiṣyasi parāṃ gatim
english: Offer sacrifice with the Sarvamedha and the Aśvamedha, O joy of the Kurus; then afterwards, O great king, you will attain the supreme goal.

sanskrit: bhrātṝṃś ca sarvān kratubhiḥ saṃyojya bahudakṣiṇaiḥ saṃprāptaḥ kīrtim atulāṃ pāṇḍaveya bhaviṣyasi
english: And having joined all your brothers in sacrifices with abundant priestly gifts, you will win unequalled fame, O scion of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: vidma te puruṣavyāghra vacanaṃ kurunandana śṛṇu mac ca yathā kurvan dharmān na cyavate nṛpaḥ
english: We know your mind, O tiger among men, O joy of the Kurus; but hear me now, how a king, acting thus, falls not away from righteousness.

sanskrit: ādadānasya ca dhanaṃ nigrahaṃ ca yudhiṣṭhira samānaṃ dharmakuśalāḥ sthāpayanti nareśvara
english: For one who seizes wealth and one who restrains the wicked, those skilled in righteousness reckon the merit equal, O lord of men, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: deśakālapratīkṣe yo dasyor darśayate nṛpaḥ śāstrajāṃ buddhim āsthāya nainasā sa hi yujyate
english: The king who, awaiting the right place and time, shows toward the robber the wisdom born of the scriptures—he is not stained by any sin.

sanskrit: ādāya baliṣaḍbhāgaṃ yo rāṣṭraṃ nābhirakṣati pratigṛhṇāti tat pāpaṃ caturthāṃśena pārthivaḥ
english: The king who takes the sixth part of the harvest as his due yet does not protect the realm—that prince takes upon himself a fourth part of all the people's sin.

sanskrit: nibodha ca yathātiṣṭhan dharmān na cyavate nṛpaḥ nigrahād dharmaśāstrāṇām anurudhyann apetabhīḥ kāmakrodhāv anādṛtya piteva samadarśanaḥ
english: Learn, too, how a king, standing thus, falls not away from righteousness: by restraining the wicked in conformity with the books of law, free from fear, heedless of desire and anger, even-eyed toward all like a father.

sanskrit: daivenopahate rājā karmakāle mahādyute pramādayati tat karma na tatrāhur atikramam
english: When, O greatly resplendent one, fate strikes the king at the moment of action and causes that act to fail, in that case they declare no transgression on his part.

sanskrit: tarasā buddhipūrvaṃ vā nigrāhyā eva śatravaḥ pāpaiḥ saha na saṃdadhyād rāṣṭraṃ paṇyaṃ na kārayet
english: By force or by stratagem the enemies must surely be subdued. He should make no pact with the wicked, nor put the kingdom up for sale.

sanskrit: śūrāś cāryāś ca satkāryā vidvāṃsaś ca yudhiṣṭhira gomato dhaninaś caiva paripālyā viśeṣataḥ
english: The brave, the noble, and the learned are to be honoured, O Yudhiṣṭhira; and those rich in cattle and in wealth are to be protected with especial care.

sanskrit: vyavahāreṣu dharmyeṣu niyojyāś ca bahuśrutāḥ guṇayukte 'pi naikasmin viśvasyāc ca vicakṣaṇaḥ
english: In the conduct of lawful affairs the deeply learned are to be appointed; yet the discerning man should not place his whole trust in any single person, however endowed with virtues.

sanskrit: arakṣitā durvinīto mānī stabdho 'bhyasūyakaḥ enasā yujyate rājā durdānta iti cocyate
english: A king who fails to protect, who is ill-disciplined, vain, unbending, and envious, is bound to sin and is called untamed.

sanskrit: ye 'rakṣyamāṇā hīyante daivenopahate nṛpe taskaraiś cāpi hanyante sarvaṃ tad rājakilbiṣam
english: When the king is struck down by fate, those who, going unprotected, perish and are slain by thieves—all that is the king's guilt.

sanskrit: sumantrite sunīte ca vidhivac copapādite pauruṣe karmaṇi kṛte nāsty adharmo yudhiṣṭhira
english: When the counsel has been good, the policy sound, and the manly deed accomplished duly as prescribed, there is no unrighteousness, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: vipadyante samārambhāḥ sidhyanty api ca daivataḥ kṛte puruṣakāre tu nainaḥ spṛśati pārthivam
english: Undertakings come to ruin, and they also succeed, by fate; but when human effort has been made, no sin touches the prince.

sanskrit: atra te rājaśārdūla vartayiṣye kathām imām yad vṛttaṃ pūrvarājarṣer hayagrīvasya pārthiva
english: On this matter, O tiger among kings, I shall relate to you this tale—what befell the ancient royal sage Hayagrīva, O prince.

sanskrit: śatrūn hatvā hatasyājau śūrasyākliṣṭakarmaṇaḥ asahāyasya dhīrasya nirjitasya yudhiṣṭhira
english: He slew his foes and was himself slain in the fray—that hero of untiring deeds, steadfast and without an ally, at last overcome, O Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: yat karma vai nigrahe śātravāṇāṃ; yogaś cāgryaḥ pālane mānavānām kṛtvā karma prāpya kīrtiṃ suyuddhe; vājigrīvo modate devaloke
english: Having done the deed of subduing his foes and exercised the highest skill in protecting his people—having done his work and won renown in noble battle—Vājigrīva rejoices now in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: saṃtyaktātmā samareṣv ātatāyī; śastraiś chinno dasyubhir ardyamānaḥ aśvagrīvaḥ karmaśīlo mahātmā; saṃsiddhātmā modate devaloke
english: Heedless of his own life, drawing his bow in the battles, cut down by weapons and beset by marauders—Aśvagrīva, devoted to his duty, that great soul made perfect, rejoices in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: dhanur yūpo raśanā jyā śaraḥ sruk; sruvaḥ khaḍgo rudhiraṃ yatra cājyam ratho vedī kāmago yuddham agniś; cāturhotraṃ caturo vājimukhyāḥ
english: The bow was his sacrificial post, the string his cord, the arrow his ladle, the sword his oblation-spoon, the blood his clarified butter; the chariot, swift as thought, his altar, the battle his fire, and the four chief steeds his four officiating priests.

sanskrit: hutvā tasmin yajñavahnāv athārīn; pāpān mukto rājasiṃhas tarasvī prāṇān hutvā cāvabhṛthe raṇe sa; vājigrīvo modate devaloke
english: Having offered his foes into that sacrificial fire, the swift lion among kings was freed from sin; and having offered up his own life-breaths in the final ablution of the battle, Vājigrīva rejoices in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: rāṣṭraṃ rakṣan buddhipūrvaṃ nayena; saṃtyaktātmā yajñaśīlo mahātmā sarvāṃl lokān vyāpya kīrtyā manasvī; vājigrīvo modate devaloke
english: Guarding the realm with deliberate, wise policy, heedless of his own life, ever devoted to sacrifice, that great soul, pervading all the worlds with his fame—the thoughtful Vājigrīva rejoices in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: daivīṃ siddhiṃ mānuṣīṃ daṇḍanītiṃ; yoganyāyaiḥ pālayitvā mahīṃ ca tasmād rājā dharmaśīlo mahātmā; hayagrīvo modate svargaloke
english: Cherishing the divine accomplishment and the human science of statecraft, and guarding the earth by the rules of right policy—therefore the king Hayagrīva, that great soul devoted to righteousness, rejoices in the world of heaven.

sanskrit: vidvāṃs tyāgī śraddadhānaḥ kṛtajñas; tyaktvā lokaṃ mānuṣaṃ karma kṛtvā medhāvināṃ viduṣāṃ saṃmatānāṃ; tanutyajāṃ lokam ākramya rājā
english: Learned, liberal, full of faith, and grateful—having forsaken the world of men once his deeds were done, the king has won the realm of the wise, the discerning, the honoured, those who lay down their bodies in battle.

sanskrit: samyag vedān prāpya śāstrāṇy adhītya; samyag rāṣṭraṃ pālayitvā mahātmā cāturvarṇyaṃ sthāpayitvā svadharme; vājigrīvo modate devaloke
english: Having duly received the Vedas and studied the scriptures, having rightly protected his realm, that great soul—having established the four orders each in its own duty—Vājigrīva rejoices in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: jitvā saṃgrāmān pālayitvā prajāś ca; somaṃ pītvā tarpayitvā dvijāgryān yuktyā daṇḍaṃ dhārayitvā prajānāṃ; yuddhe kṣīṇo modate devaloke
english: Having won his battles and protected his subjects, having drunk the soma and gratified the foremost of the twice-born, having justly wielded the rod of punishment over his people—spent in battle, he rejoices in the world of the gods.

sanskrit: vṛttaṃ yasya ślāghanīyaṃ manuṣyāḥ; santo vidvāṃsaś cārhayanty arhaṇīyāḥ svargaṃ jitvā vīralokāṃś ca gatvā; siddhiṃ prāptaḥ puṇyakīrtir mahātmā
english: He whose conduct men praise, whom the good and the learned, themselves worthy of honour, hold in honour—having won heaven and gone to the realms of heroes, that great soul of holy fame has attained perfection.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca dvaipāyanavacaḥ śrutvā kupite ca dhanaṃjaye vyāsam āmantrya kaunteyaḥ pratyuvāca yudhiṣṭhiraḥ
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Having heard the words of Dvaipāyana, and Dhanaṃjaya being still wroth, Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, addressed Vyāsa and replied to him.

sanskrit: na pārthivam idaṃ rājyaṃ na ca bhogāḥ pṛthagvidhāḥ prīṇayanti mano me 'dya śoko māṃ nardayaty ayam
english: Neither this earthly kingdom nor enjoyments of every kind give any joy to my mind today; this grief roars within me and rends me.

sanskrit: śrutvā ca vīrahīnānām aputrāṇāṃ ca yoṣitām paridevayamānānāṃ śāntiṃ nopalabhe mune
english: And hearing the women who, bereft of their heroes and their sons, wail in their lamentation, I can find no peace, O sage.

sanskrit: ity uktaḥ pratyuvācedaṃ vyāso yogavidāṃ varaḥ yudhiṣṭhiraṃ mahāprājñaṃ dharmajño vedapāragaḥ
english: Thus addressed, Vyāsa, the best of those skilled in yoga, knower of duty and master of the Vedas, made this reply to the deeply wise Yudhiṣṭhira:

sanskrit: na karmaṇā labhyate cintayā vā; nāpy asya dātā puruṣasya kaś cit paryāyayogād vihitaṃ vidhātrā; kālena sarvaṃ labhate manuṣyaḥ
english: Not by action is it gained, nor by anxious thought; nor is there any giver of it to a man. By the working of succession it has been ordained by the Ordainer: in due time a man obtains all things.

sanskrit: na buddhiśāstrādhyayanena śakyaṃ; prāptuṃ viśeṣair manujair akāle mūrkho 'pi prāpnoti kadā cid arthān; kālo hi kāryaṃ prati nirviśeṣaḥ
english: Not by intellect, nor by study of the scriptures, nor by their special gifts can men attain anything out of its season; yet even a fool at times obtains his ends, for time draws no distinction in respect of what is to be accomplished.

sanskrit: nābhūtikāle ca phalaṃ dadāti; śilpaṃ na mantrāś ca tathauṣadhāni tāny eva kālena samāhitāni; sidhyanti cedhyanti ca bhūtikāle
english: Out of the time of fruition, craft yields no result, nor do spells, nor medicines; yet those very same, gathered together by time, succeed and prosper when the season of fruition comes.

sanskrit: kālena śīghrāḥ pravivānti vātāḥ; kālena vṛṣṭir jaladān upaiti kālena padmotpalavaj jalaṃ ca; kālena puṣyanti nagā vaneṣu
english: In due time the swift winds blow forth; in due time the rain comes to the clouds; in due time the water bears its lotuses and lilies; and in due time the trees put forth their blossoms in the forests.

sanskrit: kālena kṛṣṇāś ca sitāś ca rātryaḥ; kālena candraḥ paripūrṇabimbaḥ nākālataḥ puṣpaphalaṃ nagānāṃ; nākālavegāḥ sarito vahanti
english: In due time the nights grow dark and bright again; in due time the moon comes to its full orb. Not out of season do the trees bear flower and fruit; not out of season do the rivers run with swollen flood.
